articles.title: Trams Cancelled Between Oldham and Rochdale for Two Weeks Due to Major Works
articles.excerpt: All tram services between Oldham and Rochdale will be suspended for nearly two weeks as part of significant Metrolink upgrades, with a replacement bus service provided for affected passengers.
articles.content_html:
All tram services between Oldham and Rochdale will be cancelled for almost two weeks as major engineering works are carried out on the Metrolink lines. The closure began on Monday, August 17, and will last until Friday, August 28, affecting stops including Shaw, Newhey, and Milnrow.

The suspension follows a weekend of full closure on the Rochdale line, during which track renewal works were undertaken. This is part of a £150 million upgrade to the Metrolink network, described as the largest in its history. Previous closures in July affected the Eccles, Trafford Centre, and Altrincham lines for similar upgrades.

A replacement bus service will be available for passengers holding tram tickets, as Transport for Greater Manchester (TfGM) aims to mitigate the impact of the closure. Ian Davies, network director for Metrolink, expressed gratitude to passengers for their patience during these disruptions and assured that feedback regarding the reliability of replacement buses would be taken into account for future phases of work.

Passengers are advised to plan their journeys accordingly during this period of disruption. The upgrades are expected to enhance the overall reliability and efficiency of the Metrolink service in the long term.

articles.title: Lift Out of Service at Derker Tram Stop Until Further Notice
articles.excerpt: The lift at Derker tram stop is currently out of service, affecting step-free access for passengers. Alternative routes are available for those travelling towards and away from Manchester.
articles.content_html:
The lift at Derker tram stop has been out of service since 7:23pm on 16 August 2026 and will remain unavailable until further notice. This disruption affects accessibility for passengers using the tram service.

For customers travelling towards Manchester, step-free access is available via a ramp from Cromford Street directly to the Manchester-bound platform. Passengers heading away from Manchester can also use a ramp from Cromford Street and must cross the tracks to access the Rochdale-bound platform.

Transport for Greater Manchester has apologised for any inconvenience caused by this disruption. Passengers are advised to plan their journeys accordingly and consider alternative routes if necessary.

For further information, visit the Transport for Greater Manchester website.
